comparator.name: Communication and Information Studies (Communicatie- en Informatiewetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 OER, Media en Journalistiek annual programme, checked 2026-09-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized registry target is Dutch-taught. The 2026–27 adopted OER identifies Media en Journalistiek as the sole Dutch-taught route; Language and Media and Applied Linguistics are English-taught. Its annual programme has ten 6-EC credited units in each of years one and two, 30 EC of genuinely open academic profiling space, three named 6-EC year-three units, a 3-EC thesis colloquium and a 9-EC bachelor thesis. Zero-credit orientation modules and the diagnostic Dutch test are excluded. The VU public page also lists projected 2027–28 and 2028–29 titles, which do not replace the adopted 2026–27 schedule. Journalism production in text and video and the required thesis are distinctive; the open elective space is not filled with assumed courses.
components: Genuinely open profiling period; a permitted minor, approved electives or an internship plus electives under the 2026–27 regulations.

routeSelection.basis: The registry target is Dutch-taught, and the adopted 2026–27 OER names Media en Journalistiek as the only current Dutch-taught specialization. The two English routes and closed teach-out routes do not match this target; the selection follows formal target identity, not UCR fit.

core: Media and journalism as social practices across platforms, audiences and democratic life
Critical analysis and production of journalistic texts, images and narratives
Language, rhetoric, discourse and persuasion in media communication
Empirical research on media use, effects and data journalism
adjacent: Public communication, democracy, framing, misinformation and reliable information
Visual, digital and newsroom storytelling across platforms
Communication in organizations and with different audiences
questions: How do media narratives, texts and images shape public understanding?
How can journalism investigate claims and communicate reliable information?
How do organizations communicate with audiences across changing media?

alternatives.label: Media, journalism and public storytelling
alternatives.concept: Studies media and journalism through communication, rhetoric, textual and visual narratives, audience research and democratic contexts. UCR offers related critical and practical work but does not reproduce VU’s Dutch journalism skills sequence, data-journalism specialization or bachelor thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines media analysis, writing and documentary practice, communication and social research; it is broader than a single journalism craft.
progression: Verified the fixed Fall 2026–Spring 2029 schedule against the GitHub enriched UCR course workbook: six four-course semesters, at least six 300-level courses, PPD in Year 1, term offerings and prior formal prerequisites all pass. Introductory media, rhetoric and research courses generally precede advanced work.

alternatives.label: Public communication, trust and contested information
alternatives.concept: Concentrates on persuasion, social influence, public institutions, civic trust and contested media claims. It shifts from narrative craft and media genres toward understanding how public messages gain credibility and shape democratic discussion.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum adds social psychology, political argument, EU public institutions and contested climate messages to its media and communication base.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses change from the media-storytelling curriculum: political philosophy, social psychology, EU politics and climate communication replace media-and-environment, introductory literary narrative, film/text study and narrative nonfiction. The direction studies public trust and persuasion as organizing questions rather than merely changing a title.

selection.assessment: The first curriculum provides the closest feasible response across VU media and journalism, including visual and narrative production. The public-communication route has a distinct question and at least four consequential course changes. A further visual/digital journalism idea is already substantially represented in the closest route; forcing a third would rearrange media courses without a genuinely new organizing curriculum.

notes.text: The VU Dutch-taught Media en Journalistiek route requires journalistic writing and video production, data journalism, communication-effects research and a 9-EC thesis with a 3-EC colloquium, while preserving a 30-EC open elective period. UCR can combine media, rhetoric, narrative, social research and documentary courses, but does not reproduce that structured journalism sequence or its independent thesis.
